summary: Early 429 rejects when bulk-embed flushes classified as low-latency traffic (route classification mismatch)
description:
Issue summary: BrightCart reports a spike of 429s starting 2026-03-09 17:00 UTC during nightly bulk-embed flushes. The requests are bulk ingestion jobs that should be treated as background/low-priority, but the ingress appears to classify them as low-latency interactive traffic and they hit a tight per-route concurrency window. Impact: ~35% failed batch shards (429s) for the BrightCart dedicated pool for ~45 minutes; downstream retry loops amplified the pattern.

Observed at: prod (us-east) dedicated pool for BrightCart; many requests originate from a long-running ingest worker that issues multiplexed /v1/embeds/bulk calls with chunked payloads and a custom header X-BC-JobId.
impact: Customer ingest pipeline experiencing partial failure (35% shard failures) for nightly index updates; retries caused delays and invoiceable errors. Not a full outage but customer SLA for bulk ingest throughput violated.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) In BrightCart staging/dedicated mimic: spawn 200 concurrent workers performing multiplexed chunked POST to /v1/embeds/bulk with Content-Type: multipart/form-data and X-Client-Job: bulk-flush
2) Set per-worker short timeout/fast retry loop (1s backoff) to surface early 429s
3) Observe rate-limiter accounting: per-route token window for "interactive" lane drops to zero and returns 429
4) Compare requests when header X-Redwood-Traffic-Class: background is set -> no 429s; when header missing -> 429s reproduced
observed_behavior: Requests for the same job are alternately accepted or rejected depending on a normalized route key lookup. In many cases the route used for accounting is the interactive path (/v1/chat/completions) because the gateway normalization step failed for multipart bulk embeds; this causes them to consume from a small low-latency concurrency bucket and return 429s.
expected_behavior: Bulk-embed flushes should be classified automatically into the background/bulk quota pool based on path pattern or explicit X-Redwood-Traffic-Class header; they should not be counted against short-lived interactive concurrency windows and should tolerate higher burst without early 429s.
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: rate-limiter atomic key computed from canonicalized route ID. Edge proxy change in v1.14.2 introduced a path-normalization regression: multipart requests with Content-Type multipart/form-data lost the request.path suffix during header rewrite, producing an empty route match and falling back to default route id -> mapped to 'interactive' lane. Evidence: request traces in zipkin show route_id: 'interactive-v1' for bulk embeds between 2026-03-09 17:01 and 17:45.

Telemetry: rate-limiter logs show a spike in per-route token-exhaustion events (window_exhausted) matching BrightCart tenant_id. Heap of retries from orchestrator increased queue depth by 3x.

Reproduction in staging: toggling header X-Redwood-Traffic-Class allowed bypass; canonicalizing request.path in proxy removed the regression locally and eliminated 429s.

Related: this intersects with priority-routing changes rolled out 2026-03-08 (edge proxy v1.14.2) – see PR #4321 and the rollout notes.
logs: [2026-03-09T17:02:11Z] tenant=brightcart tid=tb-11 route_id=interactive-v1 window_exhausted tokens_left=0 request_id=rc-7f2a
[2026-03-09T17:02:12Z] tenant=brightcart tid=tb-11 decision=reject status=429 reason=per_route_window_exhausted request_path=/v1/embeds/bulk content_type= multipart/form-data
comments: Support (Aisha): Customer first reported 2026-03-09 18:10 UTC. Provided sample request IDs and timeframe. Asked for logs and tenant/lb mappings.

SRE (Diego): Reproduced in staging; observed path normalization regression in edge proxy. Temporary mitigation: add X-Redwood-Traffic-Class=background in customer integration; follow-up patch to proxy in progress.

Customer (BrightCart - Rajesh Kumar): We pushed a hotfix to add the header but would prefer the platform to not require header workarounds. This nightly job is scheduled and we cannot change it in prod quickly.

Eng (Kim, gateway): Confirmed bug in v1.14.2: header rewrite step strips path suffix for multipart in a small set of connectors. PR opened to fix: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4321
SRE (Diego): Rolling forward a proxy patch to the dedicated pool (canary) and enabling a temporary route-level exemption to enlarge interactive window for BrightCart till patch completes.
resolution_notes:
Workaround applied 2026-03-10 02:00 UTC: support added a route-level exemption for tenant 'brightcart' to increase interactive concurrency window and avoid early 429s. Customer also updated their integrated job to send X-Redwood-Traffic-Class=background for nightly flushes (non-disruptive).

Permanent fix: gateway PR #4321 merged (normalizes request.path for multipart rewrites) and deployed to staging. Scheduled rollout to production dedicated pools on 2026-03-13 with phased canary. After deployment, monitored ingest for two nightly cycles; 429s did not recur.

Post-deploy: removed temporary route exemption on 2026-03-14 after verification.
follow_up_actions: 1) Backport canonicalization fix to earlier edge proxy branches (v1.13.x) used by older dedicated fleets
2) Add unit test to ensure multipart/form-data preserves path suffix during header rewrite
3) Add a diagnostic metric: route_normalization_failure_count per tenant
4) Update support runbook: if customer reports bulk-embed 429s, verify X-Redwood-Traffic-Class and route_id in trace
